title: macos: show which clause is being converted while typing Japanese
body: This PR is about how Ghostty displays Japanese text while it is being converted, which I raised in discussion #14737. When I type Japanese, the input method first shows the text I typed as text that is not yet committed. In this PR, I call it the composing text. The input method splits the composing text into clauses (short groups of words) and converts one clause at a time. The input method sends the composing text to Ghostty with two kinds of underline attributes: a thin underline for the whole composing text and a thick underline for the clause being converted. Ghostty discards these underline attributes and draws one thin underline under the whole composing text. Because of this, I cannot see which clause will change when I press the space key or the arrow keys. With this PR, Ghostty keeps the underline attributes. Ghostty draws the clause being converted with a thick underline and the rest of the composing text with a dotted underline. This PR does not add a configuration option. When no clause is marked, Ghostty displays the composing text the same way as before. This includes text that is still being typed as kana: Apple's Japanese input method puts a thick underline under all of that text, so a thick underline under the whole composing text is not treated as a clause. ### Screenshots In both screenshots, the composing text is 今日はいい天気です ("It is nice weather today"), and the clause being converted is いい ("nice"). This PR (a dotted underline for the composing text and a thick underline for the clause being converted): Another option that I tried (a thin underline for the composing text and a thick underline for the clause being converted): With the thin underline and the thick underline, the difference is hard to see. Personally, I found the combination of the dotted underline and the thick underline easier to read, so I chose the dotted underline. If you prefer the thin underline, the change is one line in the function `addPreeditCell` in `src/renderer/generic.zig`. ### Changes - macOS app (`SurfaceView_AppKit.swift`): `validAttributesForMarkedText` returns `[.underlineStyle]`, so AppKit no longer removes the underline attributes. The macOS app finds the range with the thick underline and passes the range to the Ghostty core through a new C API function, `ghostty_surface_preedit_selected`. The existing function `ghostty_surface_preedit` does not change. - Ghostty core (`Surface.zig`, `renderer/State.zig`): each codepoint of the composing text gets a `selected` flag that is true when the codepoint is in the clause being converted. - Renderer (`renderer/generic.zig`): when the composing text has a clause being converted, the renderer draws that clause with a new `underline_thick` sprite and the other codepoints with the existing `underline_dotted` sprite. - Linux version (GTK): the GTK code passes no range, so the GTK version does not change. - Tests (`SurfaceViewAppKitTests.swift`): new cases check the range that the macOS app finds, for example a clause after an emoji, a double underline, and a thick underline under the whole text. ### Testing - All Ghostty tests (`zig build test -Dxcframework-target=native`), including the macOS app tests, pass on the current `main`. - On macOS 27.0.1, Claude Code built the app and used a script to type Japanese in a Ghostty window with Apple's Japanese input method and with one other Japanese input method, and took screenshots. It checked typing kana, converting, moving between clauses, changing the length of a clause, going back to kana, committing, a single clause, and composing text that is wider than the window. - It also typed with Apple's Korean (2-Set) and Chinese (Pinyin) input methods. They do not use a thick underline, and their composing text looks the same as before. - Finally, I typed Japanese in the built app myself and confirmed that the clause being converted has a thick underline and the rest has a dotted underline. ### AI disclosure I am not a developer, and my native language is Japanese. I used Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) for this PR. I decided what to change and how it should look. Claude Code read the Ghostty code to find the cause, wrote the code and the tests, ran the tests, and took the screenshots with a script. Claude Code also wrote the English of this text, and I checked it with Google Translate.

+import AppKit
 @testable import Ghostty
 import Testing
 
@@ -41,4 +42,41 @@ struct SurfaceViewAppKitTests {
             ) == false
         )
     }
+
+    /// Marked text with the given underline styles; each run is
+    /// (UTF-16 location, UTF-16 length, NSUnderlineStyle raw value).
+    private func marked(_ text: String, _ runs: [(Int, Int, Int)]) -> NSAttributedString {
+        let s = NSMutableAttributedString(string: text)
+        for (loc, len, style) in runs {
+            s.addAttribute(.underlineStyle, value: style, range: NSRange(location: loc, length: len))
+        }
+        return s
+    }
+
+    @Test(arguments: [
+        // No underline, or a thin one only (e.g. kana being typed).
+        ("今日は", [], 0..<0),
+        ("今日は", [(0, 3, 0x1)], 0..<0),
+        // Thick over all of the text (Apple's input method while typing kana).
+        ("きょうは", [(0, 4, 0x2)], 0..<0),
+        // A clause in the middle, at the start and at the end.
+        ("今日はいい天気です", [(0, 3, 0x1), (3, 2, 0x2), (5, 4, 0x1)], 9..<15),
+        ("今日はいい天気です", [(0, 3, 0x2), (3, 6, 0x1)], 0..<9),
+        ("今日はいい天気です", [(0, 5, 0x1), (5, 4, 0x2)], 15..<27),
+        // ASCII and an emoji (two UTF-16 units, four UTF-8 bytes) before it.
+        ("a😀いい", [(0, 3, 0x1), (3, 2, 0x2)], 5..<11),
+        // Thick with a pattern, double is not thick, the first thick wins.
+        ("いい天気", [(0, 2, 0x2 | 0x100), (2, 2, 0x1)], 0..<6),
+        ("いい天気", [(0, 2, 0x9), (2, 2, 0x1)], 0..<0),
+        ("いい天気", [(0, 1, 0x2), (1, 1, 0x1), (2, 1, 0x2), (3, 1, 0x1)], 0..<3),
+    ])
+    func findsSelectedClauseUTF8Range(
+        text: String,
+        runs: [(Int, Int, Int)],
+        expected: Range<Int>
+    ) {
+        #expect(
+            Ghostty.SurfaceView.selectedClauseUTF8Range(marked(text, runs)) == expected
+        )
+    }
 }

 }
 
+pub fn underline_thick(
+    cp: u32,
+    canvas: *font.sprite.Canvas,
+    width: u32,
+    height: u32,
+    metrics: font.Metrics,
+) !void {
+    _ = cp;
+
+    // Twice the usual thickness, grown upward from the usual underline
+    // position so it stays within the canvas like the single underline.
+    const thick = 2 * metrics.underline_thickness;
+    const y = @min(
+        metrics.underline_position,
+        height +| canvas.padding_y -| metrics.underline_thickness,
+    ) -| metrics.underline_thickness;
+
+    canvas.rect(.{
+        .x = 0,
+        .y = @intCast(y),
+        .width = @intCast(width),
+        .height = @intCast(thick),
+    }, .on);
+}
